context: Animated phyllotaxis data art: 2000 dots (default) arranged on a golden-angle spiral with oscillating angle perturbation and radius breathing, rendered on canvas via 3 additive-blend passes per frame. Controls for dot count (200–5000), angle offset, speed, dot size, and 5 palette choices.
first_impression: Elegant and minimal — a single circular structure with low cognitive demand, though the dots are very dim at default settings and the visual impact depends heavily on the animation that can't be assessed from a static screenshot.
what_works: Cognitive load is near-zero: one conceptual structure, one view, no data encoding to decode, and controls are well-labeled and non-intrusive. The 3-palette-pass glow technique and additive compositing are well-suited to data art and avoid color overload by keeping one active palette at a time.
what_doesnt: At default settings (2000 dots, ocean palette) alpha scales to ~0.08 per pass, making dots extremely faint in the screenshot — the glow effect likely only reads well in motion with additive blending, so the static state underwhelms. Animation quality (oscillation, breathing, pointer repulsion on 6000 draw ops/frame) cannot be assessed from the screenshot and is the primary perceptual risk.
